title: What Makes Medical Examination Items Difficult? Using Large Language Models to Explore Patterns Associated With Empirical Item Difficulty
abstract: arXiv:2610.39373v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Research on medical item difficulty has largely focused on prediction rather than on identifying interpretable patterns associated with empirical difficulty. This study used empirical difficulty labels to guide large language models (LLMs) in inducing difficulty rubrics and examined how rubric guidance affected LLM difficulty judgments. Using training items and their empirical difficulty estimates from the United States Medical Licensing Examination (USMLE) and the Physician Assistant National Certifying Examination (PANCE), Claude Opus 5 induced separate rubrics for absolute and pairwise difficulty judgment. None of the induced rubrics treated surface features, such as stem length, option count, or images, as major sources of difficulty. translated_title: 是什么让医学考试题目变得困难？利用大语言模型探索与经验性题目难度相关的模式
translated_abstract: arXiv:2610.39373v1 公告类型：交叉 摘要：关于医学考试题目难度的研究大多集中于难度预测，而非识别与经验性难度相关的可解释模式。本研究使用经验性难度标签来引导大语言模型（LLMs）归纳难度评分规则，并考察了评分规则引导如何影响大语言模型的难度判断。研究使用了美国医师执照考试（USMLE）和助理医师国家认证考试（PANCE）的训练题目及其经验性难度估计，由Claude Opus 5分别为绝对难度判断和成对比较难度判断归纳了不同的评分规则。所有归纳出的评分规则均未将表面特征（如题干长度、选项数量或图像）视为难度的主要来源。两项考试中均出现了若干共同模式，包括线索趋同、误导性线索和选项竞争，尽管它们的具体表现形式有所不同。无法被……
tldr: 本研究利用医学考试题目的经验性难度标签引导大语言模型归纳难度评分规则，发现题目难度主要源于线索趋同、误导性线索和选项竞争等深层模式，而非题干长度、选项数量等表面特征。
en_tdlr: This study used empirical difficulty labels from medical licensing exams to guide LLMs in inducing difficulty rubrics, revealing that item difficulty stems from deeper patterns such as cue convergence, misleading cues, and option competition rather than surface features like stem length or option count.
